In a sojourner and in a native of the Land () = those who are of the Church, whether not born therein or whether born therein.
They who are of the Church, but not within it, as the Gentiles who live together in obedience and mutual charity...

He who when instructed receives the truth and good of the Church and lives according to it, shall be as he who had been instructed before within the Church and had lived a life conformable to the precepts of faith and charity. Signified.
The Church is in those who have charity and faith.

Those with whom faith is separated from its good, both as to doctrine and as to life... are not of this Church, for life makes the Church, and not doctrine except in so far as it is of life. Hence it is evident, that the Lord's Church is not here or there, but that it is everywhere, both within those kingdoms where the Church is, and outside of them, where men live according to the commandments of charity. Hence it is that the Lord's Church is scattered through the universal world, and yet is one; for when life makes the Church, and not doctrine separated from life, the Church is one; but when doctrine makes the Church, there are many.
His throne = Heaven and the Church.

In falsities and at the same time in good are those within the Church who are in heresies and the life of good; and so are all outside the Church who are in good; but falsities with these do not condemn...

The end of the Church is here treated of, when what is external, thus what is sensuous and corporeal, and together with these what is false and evil have the dominion, for the Lord's Church advances successively to what is external, and then expires.
He acknowledges it to be true because the Church has said so.
A sojourner = those who are born outside the Church, and yet were instructed in the things of the Church.
The Lord's Church is scattered through the whole world, thus is also with the Gentiles. References.
Eliezer () = the quality of the good of truth with those who are within the Church. Explained.
The mercy and presence of the Lord in the Church. Signified, Explained.
These things are the essentials of the Church, and cause it to be the Church...
With everyone who is of the Church, there must be both... what is external and what is internal. Explained.
For there to be a Church there must be with the man of the Church faith in the Lord and also love to Him and love towards the neighbour; these things make the Church.
World () = the Church.
Under Kingdom of the Lord, see this reference.
The last time of the Church, treated of. AC 8902:6. AC 8902:8. AC 8906:2. AC 9139:5. AC 9141:end. AC 9348:9. AE 39. AE 486.
The Church is at its end...
Therefore they divide the Church into so many Churches...

The Lord's Church is with everyone who is in a state of reception of charity and faith from the Lord; for the man himself is the Church, and a number with whom the Church is make the Church in general.
Those within the Church who are in truths of doctrine and not in good according thereto. Signified, Explained.
The marriage of good and truth is the Church itself, because it is Heaven in man. References.
The Church is now predicated and called from faith and not from charity...
Love to the Lord and towards the neighbour is the being itself of Heaven and the Church, and faith is the manifesting thence. AC 9032.
A strange people () = those who are outside the Church, thus those who are not of the faith of the Church.

They who are have been born within the Church, and from infancy have imbued the principles of the truth of the Church, ought not to contract marriages with those who are outside the Church, and thus imbue such things as are not of the Church. Explained.
The Church is called a forest from knowledge, a garden from intelligence, and a paradise from wisdom.
Thorough and complete denial of the Lord and His Kingdom by those who are of the Church. Signified.
They who are within the Church can profane holy things, but not they who are outside the Church. References.
The good in which truths are thus implanted is the Church with man.
By the prior state (of regeneration) man is introduced into the Church in order to become the Church, and when he has become the Church he is in the latter state.
The Church is the Lord's Heaven or Kingdom on earth. AC 10304. AC 10446.
This state is the last state of the Church, the former is its first state.
Many of those who are in the Church cannot be withheld from (profanation). Explained.
To be cast out of the Church. Signified.
No prophet is accepted in his own country () = that the Lord and the Divine truth which is from Him is less received and loved at heart within the Church than without it.
The poor and needy = those who, outside the Church, are in ignorance of truth... and within the Church, those who from various causes are ignorant of truth but still from some good yearn for it.
The Church at this day is in internal truths.
The Lord always provides that there be a Church with mankind in which Divine truth is revealed, which in our Earth is the Word... AC 9276:7.
The first thing of all with the man of the Church is to believe the Word...
Their giving the first fruits to Jehovah, signified that it was the first of the Church to ascribe all the goods and truths of faith to the Lord, and not to themselves...
The two disputes which, from primeval times, have infested the Church. Explained.
The good of charity is the principal of the Church...
The rich man = those within the Church... The poor man = those who within the Church are in but little good in consequence of their ignorance of truth, but still yearn to be instructed. AC 10227:20.
Good and truth not genuine with those who are outside the Church. Signified, Explained. In the other life they live separate from those who are of the Church...
Good is to be done to those who are outside the Church. Signified.

Therefore the Lord's Church is scattered through the whole world; but the Lord's Church itself on earth is as the Grand Man in the Heavens, whose heart and lungs are where the Word is, and the rest of the members and viscera, which live from the heart and lungs, are where the Word is not. AC 9400:end. HH 305. [Swedenborg footnote 1.] References.

These three kinds of men constitute the Church; they who are in the good of charity constitute the internal of the Church; they who are in few truths and still want to be instructed, thus who are in the affection of truth from good, constitute the external of the Church; and they who are in the delights of external truth are the outermost, and make as it were the circumference, and close the Church. Signified.

By a man of the Church is meant one who is in the good of charity and thence in the truths of faith from the Lord, for the charity from which is faith is the Church itself with man, because they are from the Lord.
The universal Church before the Lord is as a man... AC 9276:9, References. AC 9400:end.
The man of the Church in particular is Heaven, the Church, and the Lord's Kingdom in the least effigy. AC 9276:9, References.
Without a Church on earth mankind would perish. References.
The state of life of those who are in truths and goods outside the Church. Signified, Explained.
Harvest, here, () = the last state of the Church as to the reception of the truths of faith in good.
They who have been born outside the Church, and have believed in one God, flee from those who are within the Church, saying that they believe in three gods.
Protection against and removal of the evils and falsities which infest the Church. Signified.
Everyone within the Church who has been regenerated through truth and good is a Church.
The barren = the nations which are called to the Church, and to which the Church is transferred when the old Church ceases.
The perversion and destruction of the Church after its establishment, treated of.
The establishment of the Church, treated of.
Reception in the understanding by those who are truly of the Church. Signified.

The successive states of the Church on this Earth as to the reception of truth Divine proceeding from the Lord, is meant by the image seen by Nebuchadnezzar. Explained. AC 10030:3. AR 913:3. AE 176:2, Explained.
As a house rests on its foundations, so does Heaven upon the Church... This is why it is always provided by the Lord that there be a Church on earth...
The sanctuary () = the Church; and sanctuaries = those things which are of the Church.
Heaven and the Church, or the Angels of Heaven and the men of the Church, are guarded by the Lord by the elevation of their interiors towards Himself...
The Church is called a candlestick from the Divine truth which is there from the Lord.
Habitation () = Heaven, and also the Church where the Lord is.
Those of the Church, but in falsities. Signified.
The Church will perish by faith alone. Signified.
The changes to be undergone by the Church. Signified.
The six days before the seventh = the former Church even to its end, and the establishment of a new one.
The Church through the Word from the Lord. Signified.
The mount of Olives () = the good of love and charity, thus the Church, for these goods make the Church.
The Lord's advent is the revelation of truth Divine at the end of the Church. Signified.
Heaven and the Church make one, and the Church is the Lord's Heaven on earth.
All things of doctrine and worship from good passing to those who are of the Church. Signified.
The Church which is the Church is in internal things, which are of faith and love...
They are said to be out of the Church who do not acknowledge the Lord.
They who are born within the Church, yet deny the Lord at heart, however good in moral life... cannot be saved. Signified.

Whatever represents the Lord represents Him with the men of the Church, thus represents the Church, since the men in whom the Church is, constitute the Church in general... Still the men regarded in themselves do not constitute the Church, but the Lord with them... Hence when it is said the Church... there is meant the Divine of the Lord with those who are there...

When Heaven is mentioned, the Church is also meant, for the Lord's Heaven on earth is the Church; and everyone in whom the Church is, in him also is Heaven... The Church also makes one with Heaven, for the one depends upon the other...

(The four states of the Church are meant by morning, noon, evening, and night.) When the Church is in its night, that is, when it is no longer in love to God and in faith, morning begins with another nation... AC 10134:9, Explained.
The time when the cock crew = the last state of the Church.

The men in the Church do not make the Church as to their proprium, but as to what is Divine which they receive from the Lord; for whoever therein does not acknowledge and believe that all good... and truth... are from the Lord, is not of the Church... The Church too is the Lord's Heaven on earth, hence the Lord is all in all things of the Church... and He dwells there in what is His own with men...
He therefore who within the Church does not acknowledge the Lord, has not any conjunction with the Divine... It is otherwise with those who are outside the Church...
The genuine truths and goods of faith and love exist only with those who are of the Church, because they have the Word.
The Church which places everything of the Church in naked knowledges, and on that account sets itself above others. Signified.
The preservation of the Church and of all things of the Church by the Lord. Signified. AC 10232, Explained.
The Church on this Earth has been established four times. Enumerated.
The Divine things which proceed from the Lord make the Church, and nothing whatever of man.
He who does not acknowledge the Lord is not of the Church. Signified.

They alone are of the Church in whom the Church is, and the Church is in those who are in the affection of truth for the sake of truth and in the affection of good for the sake of good, thus who are in love towards the neighbour and in love to God... Those not of this character are not of the Church, however much they are in the Church.
Those in the good of love with whom the Church is to be established. Signified.
All who are in the universal Heaven and in the universal Church. Signified.
The essentials of the Church. Enumerated.
The principal thing by which those of the Church are known in Heaven. Signified.

They who are of the Church in whom the Church is, must acknowledge the Lord and the Divine in Him, must acknowledge the conjunction of the Lord with Heaven, and also the conjunction of Heaven with the man of the Church, and in general, the conjunction of good and truth with him, for this conjunction makes the Church with him. Whether you say the Church with man, or Heaven with him, or the Kingdom of God with him, or the Lord with him, it is the same, for the Church is the Lord's Heaven on earth, and the Lord's Kingdom is Heaven and the Church together, and the Lord is their Source, nay, is them.

All the good and truth which make the Church. Signified. That these make the Church with man... is evident from the fact that love and faith are the essentials of the Church, because they conjoin men and Angels with the Lord...
That the Church is not with man, but Hell. Signified.
When man becomes a Church and enters Heaven. Signified, Explained.
By this are distinguished those who are of the Church from those who are not of the Church. Signified.
That with the Israelitish people the Church could not be instituted, because they were entirely in externals without any internal. (Treated of, in ). AC 10397. AC 10525.

The Church is not the Church from external worship, but from internal... The man of the Church communicates with the Heavens through the interior things of worship, to which what is external serves as a plane...
For the sake of Heaven and the Church. Signified.
The Church acts as one with Heaven, for the one comes forth and subsists from the other.
Duration of such worship till the end of the Church. Signified.

The Church on earth was instituted in order that there might be a communication of the world, that is, of mankind, with Heaven, that is, through Heaven with the Lord, for without a Church there would be no communication, and mankind would perish... HH 305:1, References.
That the internal of the Church, etc., should not perish. Signified.
By the Holy Supper there is conjunction of the Church with Heaven, thus with the Lord; therefore it is the most holy thing of the Church.
The Church with man is in his internal.
The Divine of the Lord, from which is the Church and its worship. Signified.
To dispose and order the things of the Church and of worship. Signified.
The tent of the assembly = the external of the Church, etc., in which are internal things.
Where the Word is, there is the Church.
If the Divine be not there, there will not be anything of the Church there. Signified.
The Divine will be in the external of the Church, etc. Signified.
The restoration of the Church. Treated of.
To close up the internal of the Church, etc. Signified.
The externals of the Church, etc., would be seen, but not the internals. Signified.

In  it treats of the Church to be instituted with the Israelitish nation; but as it was such that it could not receive the Divine from within, that nation was received in order that there might be with it the representative of the Church, and not the Church. AC 10602.
The chief things of the Church which are by all means to be observed that they might represent the Church. Treated of.
The transparency of the Divine internal of the Church, etc., through their external, but not before that nation. Signified.

Hew thee two tables of stone like the former () = the external of the Church, etc., such as it was for the sake of that nation... The Church is from the Word, for all the truth of faith and the good of love which make the Church must be from the Word: hence as in the Word there are an external and an internal, there are also an external and an internal in the Church.
The Church cannot be instituted with any people unless their interiors are open, through which there is communication with Heaven...
Still the Church may be there. Signified.
To become the Church is to receive the life of Heaven through the good of love and of faith from the Lord.
The Church where the Word is. Signified.
The truths which are from good make the Church with man.

They are in the internal of the Church, etc., who love to do truth for the sake of truth from internal affection, thus from spiritual affection; in the external of it in which there is an internal are they who love truth for the sake of truth, but from external affection, thus from natural affection; the latter are men of the external Church, the former are of the internal Church, for in every Church there are both internal and external men. But they who are in external worship without internal, love truth not for the sake of truth, but for the sake of gain in the world... these are not within the Church, but outside it.
Temptations before the internal of the Church, etc., is possible. Signified, Explained.
Influx of the internal into the external of the Church, etc. Signified.
The Church cannot exist with those who are in externals without an internal, because the Church is in what is internal of man, and not in what is external without it...
Such as is man's understanding of the Word, such is the Church in him.
The two universals on which all other things of the Church depend. Signified, Explained.
What makes Heaven with man also makes the Church, for the Church is the Lord's Heaven on earth.

It is called the Church where the Lord is acknowledged, and where the Word is; for the essentials of the Church are love and faith to and in the Lord from the Lord, and the Word teaches how man is to live in order to receive love and faith from the Lord. WH 6:3.

For there to be a Church there must be doctrine from the Word, as without doctrine the Word is not understood; but doctrine alone in man does not make the Church in him, but life according thereto; hence it follows that faith alone does not make the Church, but the life of faith which is charity.

They who are out of the Church, yet acknowledge one God, and live according to their religion in a kind of charity towards the neighbour, are in communion with those who are of the Church... Hence it is evident that the Lord's Church is everywhere in the whole world, although specifically it is where the Lord is acknowledged and where the Word is. HH 308:1, References.
Everyone with whom the Church is, is saved, but everyone with whom the Church is not is condemned.
Priests must teach men according to the doctrine of their own Church from the Word. NJHD 315.
Therefore the primary of the Church is to acknowledge God, to believe in God, and to love Him. NJHD 296.
They who are born within the Church ought to acknowledge the Lord, His Divine and His Human, and to believe in Him and love Him. Signified.
Those within the Church who do not acknowledge the Lord and His Divine cannot be conjoined with God, and thus cannot have any lot with the Angels in Heaven...
At the end of the Church the Lord will open the Word as to its internal sense, and reveal the arcana of Heaven. Signified.
They who within the Church have denied the Lord, and have acknowledged only the Father, and have confirmed themselves in such a faith, are outside Heaven...

What is said of Heaven may be said of the Church, for the Church is the Lord's Heaven on earth. There are many Churches, yet each is called a Church, and also is the Church in proportion as the good of love and of faith reigns there; therein the Lord makes one thing out of many, thus one Church out of many. What is said of the Church in general may be said of the man of the Church in particular, namely, that the Church is within man, and not without him, and that every man is a Church in whom the Lord is present in the good of love and of faith. A man in whom the Church is... is a Church in the least form; and further, a man in whom the Church is... is Heaven... HH 57. [Swedenborg footnote 3]. References.
[Swedenborg footnote 1]. If good were the mark and essential of the Church, and not truth without good, the Church would be one. References.
All Churches make one Church before the Lord from good. References.
[Swedenborg footnote 2]. The Church is in man, and not outside him; and the Church in general is from the men in whom the Church is. References.
Such ignorance is chiefly within the Church.
[Swedenborg footnote 1]. The universal Church on earth is before the Lord as one man. References. HH 308. DSS 105.

There is also conjunction of Heaven through the Word with those outside the Church, where the Word is not, for the Lord's Church is universal, and is with all who acknowledge the Divine and live in charity... HH 308. [Swedenborg footnote 1], References. DSS 104, General article.
[Swedenborg footnote 1]. The Lord's Church is with all in the whole world who live in good according to their religion, and acknowledge the Divine. References.

The Lord's Church is scattered through the whole world, thus is universal, and in it are all who have lived in the good of charity according to their religion; and the Church where the Word is... is to those outside the Church as the heart and lungs are in man...
More adulteries committed and also confirmed within the Church than outside of it.
Wisdom is to love... the good of the Church, etc.
He who is in self-love does not love the Church, etc. Explained.
He who is in self-love wants the Church, etc., to serve him...
It is provided by the Lord that there is always a Church on earth, for through the Church there is conjunction of the Lord with mankind, and of Heaven with the world... DSS 110.
The doctrine of charity then conjoined all Churches, and so made one out of many; for they acknowledged as men of the Church all who had lived in the good of charity...
The conjunction of good and truth makes the Church. DLife 32:end. AR 97:2.
Love to the Lord and love towards the neighbour make Heaven with man... and therefore they make the Church with him.
On the Church. General article. (From AC 10760.)
Love and faith make the Church.
There is a Church in the Heavens as well as on earth. AR 65.
The Last Judgment takes place when it is the end of the Church, and it is the end of the Church when there is no faith because there is no charity. General article.
The equilibrium between Heaven and Hell begins to perish at the end of the Church...
As at the end of the Church evil increases over good, all are judged by the Lord...
Within the Church faith is now so rare that...

Every Church at the beginning is spiritual, for it begins from charity, but in course of time turns aside from charity to faith, and then from an internal Church it becomes an external Church, and then is its end.
The spiritual sense treats everywhere... of the state of the Church in the Heavens and on earth.
The quality of the Church on earth cannot be seen by any man so long as he lives in the world... but it appears in Heaven as in clear day... DP 251:4.
On this Earth there have been two Churches; the first before the Flood, and the other after it.
The Church is not there, but Babylon; for the Church is where the Lord is worshipped and the Word is read.
On the state of the world and of the Church hereafter. General article. LJCont 8, General article.

The state of the Church will not be similar hereafter; it will indeed be similar as to the outward appearance, but dissimilar as to the inward; as to the outward appearance there will be divided Churches as before, and their doctrines will be taught as before... but hereafter the man of the Church will be in a freer state of thinking about the things of faith... LJ 74.
Before the Last Judgment... much of the communication between... the Lord and the Church was intercepted. Explained.
The state of the world and of the Church before the Last Judgment was as evening and night, but after it as morning and day. Explained.
They are not of the Church who are born where the Word is... but they who are regenerated by the Lord through truths from the Word. References.
The Church would be one if they were acknowledged as men of the Church from life, thus from charity. References.

The prophets represented the state of the Church and of the Word, for he who represents the one represents the other, for the Church is from the Word, and is according to the reception of it in life and faith.
It would have been all over with the Church, for the Church is the Church from the Lord.
The men of the Church in the world are in the Divine Natural, which also proceeds from the Lord. See TCR 195.
The successive states of the Church as to the understanding of the Word. Signified, Enumerated.
The state of the Church when all the knowledges of truth from the Word are destroyed. Treated of.
The Church is from the Word, and is such as is its understanding of the Word. General article.
It is not the Word which makes the Church, but the understanding of it.
In proportion as the Lord is conjoined with man is the Church in man. The Church is in man; the Church which is outside him is the Church with a number in whom is the Church. Signified.
There is no Church except where the Word is justly understood.
In each thing of the Word there is a marriage of the Lord and the Church. General article.
The spiritual sense treats chiefly of the Church; the celestial chiefly of the Lord.
The understanding is the receptacle of truth... the will of good, and these must make one for a man to be a man of the Church.

By the Lord's becoming the Word in ultimates the state of the Church was completely changed, for all the Churches before His advent were representative Churches; but after His advent a Church was instituted by Him which saw Divine truth in light... The state of the Church before His advent is called evening, and that of the Church after it morning. Explained. (See TCR 109.)

There can be no conjunction with Heaven unless there is somewhere on the Earth a Church where the Word is, and the Lord thereby known... It is enough that there be a Church where the Word is, even if it consists of comparatively few...

The universal Church is as one man before the Lord... In that man the Church where the Word is read is as the heart and lungs; the Celestial Kingdom as the heart, and the Spiritual Kingdom as the lungs.
Faith separate from charity destroys the Church and all things of it. General article.
The spiritual body is the Church, and its head is God.
It would be the same with the Church scattered through the whole world, which is called the communion...
It is the same with the man of the Church, if with him love and wisdom, or charity and faith, make one.
By a man of the Church is meant a man in whom the Church is.
Such also is the conjunction of the Lord with the Church, and of the Church with the Lord, which is called the celestial and spiritual marriage.

The Lord's Heaven in the natural world is called the Church, and an angel of this Heaven is a man of the Church who is conjoined with the Lord... Hence what is said of the angelic Heaven is understood of the human Heaven, which is called the Church.
Hatred against the Divine things of the Church.
The first kind of profanation is from those who jest from and concerning the Divine things of the Church. Explained.
Solomon was permitted to establish idolatrous worships in order to represent the Lord's Kingdom or Church with all religions in the whole world. Explained.
It is everywhere acknowledged that the Word is holy, and that the Lord has what is Divine; and these two things are the essentials of the Church...
When the Church itself assumed as its essentials such things as are only of the understanding... and when the things of life are not essentials of the Church, man is in mere darkness.

There are three essentials of the Church; the acknowledgement of the Lord's Divine, the acknowledgement of the holiness of the Word, and the life which is called charity... If these three had been regarded as the essentials of the Church, intellectual differences would not have divided, but would only have varied it...

Some opine that the Lord's Church is only in the Christian world, because the Lord is known only there, and there only is the Word; yet there are many who believe that the Lord's Church is general, or extended and scattered through the whole world... It follows that there are most general principles of the Church which enter into all religions, and make this communion. These are the acknowledgement of God and the good of life.
All who make these two universals of the Church of their life have a place in Heaven.

On this Earth there have been many Churches, one after another, for wherever mankind is, there is the Church; for... no one can come into Heaven unless he is in the two universal principles of the Church, which are to acknowledge God and live well. (The successive Churches on this Earth, and their consummations. Enumerated.)
That only those are saved who are born within the Church is an insane heresy. Explained.
The doctrines of all Churches, when regarded interiorly, teach life. Explained.
Preface. [3]. Upon a just idea of God is founded... the universal Church.
x. a. (The doctrine of the Reformed respecting the Church.)
Predictions from the Lord concerning His Church, such as it would be at its end and afterwards, both in the Heavens and on earth. AE 5.
The Revelation does not treat of the successive states of the Church... but from beginning to end, of the last state of the Church in the Heavens and on earth... AE 5.
Unless the Church were finished before its time it would utterly perish. Signified.
As the good of life from charity and its faith makes the Church, the arcana concerning the state of the Church are revealed through the apostle John.
The time is at hand = that the state of the Church is such that it can endure no longer, so as to be in conjunction with the Lord.
John to the seven Churches = to all who are in the Christian world, where the Word is, and by it the Lord known, and who accede to the Church. AR 40. AR 43.
These, if they live according to the Lord's commandments in the Word, make the Church itself.
The Church is not with man until truth becomes of the life... AR 17:end.
The Lord will reveal Himself in the sense of the letter of the Word, and open its spiritual sense at the end of the Church. Signified.
This will be when there are no longer any goods and truths in the Church. Signified.
The things in the Church which are infested by evils and falsities, but which will be removed by the Lord at His coming. Signified.
All states of the reception of the Lord and His Church are signified by these seven names.
The candlesticks were golden, because gold = good, and every Church is a Church from the good which is formed through truths.
As the Church is the Church from the Lord through the Word, the Son of Man was seen in the midst of the candlesticks.
The Church on earth is in the Divine Natural.
The seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven Churches () = the New Church on earth... The universal New Church with its varieties is described by the seven Churches.

The seven candlesticks do not mean seven Churches, but the Church in the whole complex, which in itself is one, but is varied according to reception; these varieties may be compared to the various jewels in a king's crown, and also to the various members and organs in a perfect body... Hence it is that the universal New Church with its varieties is described in what follows by the seven Churches. AR 73. AR 87.
To the Churches in the Christian world ().

The seven Churches describe all in the Christian Church who have religion, and from whom the New Church which is the New Jerusalem can be formed... The rest are indeed in the Church, but have nothing of the Church in them.
Thou hast left thy first charity () = that they do not hold goods of life in the first place, which yet has been and is done at the beginning of every Church. AE 104.

Every Church, when beginning, regards goods of life in the first place and truths of doctrine in the second, but as the Church declines it begins to regard truths of doctrine in the first place and goods of life in the second, and at last at its end it regards faith alone, and then not only separates the goods of charity from faith, but even omits them.

What the spirit saith to the Churches = what the Divine truth of the Word teaches those who will be of the New Church, which is the New Jerusalem... The Churches = the universal Church in the Christian world.
As what is written to the seven Churches describes the state of all in the Christian Church who can receive the doctrine of the New Jerusalem, and live according to it...
The Church is not the Church without doctrine. Explained.
They say the Church is with them, when yet there is no Church with them. Signified.
Truths from good from the Lord... support the Lord's Church in Heaven. Signified.
The temple, here, = the present Church; and its destruction so that there was not one stone upon another = the end of this Church...
The present state of the Church. Signified, Described.
Those in the Church, or in any religion, who are in truths as to doctrine and in goods as to life, are redeemed by the Lord. Signified.
The destruction of all the good of the Church. Signified.
The twelve tribes of Israel = the Church from those who are in good and truth from the Lord, and who acknowledge Him as the God of Heaven and earth.

Sealed from every tribe of Israel () = Heaven and the Lord's Church from them... Every tribe = the Church as to all the good of love and as to all the truth of that good, from which is the good of life; for there are two things which make the Church, the good of love and the truth of doctrine; their marriage is the Church. The twelve tribes of Israel represented the Church as to this marriage...
The universal Heaven together with the Church on earth before the Lord is as one man, and there are some who constitute the head, some the body... TCR 119, Explained.
The state of the Church with them tottering to destruction. Signified.
Lamentations over the devastation of the Church. Signified. AR 518. AE 531.
Three things make the man of the Church; the Spiritual, the Rational, and the Natural...
Those who are in a perpetual effort to take away light and spiritual life from the men of the Church. Signified.
It is by these that the men of the Church perish. Signified.
The Lord has under His auspices and dominion the universal Church, both those who are in the externals and those who are in the internals of it. Signified.
Those who are in the externals of the Church have not so confirmed falsities in themselves as those who are in its internals. Signified.
The Lord's grievous lamentation that the Church is taken from Him. Signified.
There should be time no longer () = there shall not be any state of the Church, or any Church, unless one God is acknowledged, and that the Lord is He.
The final investigation and manifestation of the state of the Church, that it will perish unless a New Church is established by the Lord. Signified.
A movement of the mind with many in the Church to receive the doctrine. Signified.
The power of seeing the state of the Church in Heaven, and in the world, given by the Lord. Signified.
These three things make the Church; the truth of doctrine, the good of love, and worship from them. Signified.
The state of the Church in Heaven before it was conjoined with the Church in the world, to be seen and known. Signified.

There is a Church in the Heavens equally as on earth, and they make one as do the internal and external with men; wherefore the Church in the Heavens is first provided by the Lord, and from or through it a Church on earth. Signified.
The state of the Church on earth... is to be removed, and not known. Signified. AE 630.
Because the state of the Church is destroyed and desolated by evils of life. Signified.
Where there is no truth there is no Church.
Love and intelligence, or charity and faith, make the Church; love and charity its life, and intelligence and faith its doctrine.
Investigation and manifestation of the state of the Church after consummation. Signified.

The reason the moon was seen under the woman's feet, is that the Church on earth which is not as yet conjoined with the Church in the Heavens, is meant... Otherwise, the feet = that Church itself, when it is conjoined.

There is a Church in the Heavens equally as on earth, for the Word is there, places of worship, preaching in them, and ministries and priesthoods... The Church with them is meant by the woman encompassed with the sun, and upon whose head there was a crown of twelve stars; and as the Church in the Heavens does not subsist unless there is also a Church on earth which is in concordant love and wisdom, and this there would be, the moon was seen under the woman's feet... The reason the Church in the Heavens does not subsist unless there is conjoined with it a Church on earth, is that Heaven where the Angels are, and the Church where men are, act as one...
By these four beasts are described the successive states of the Church...

Every Church appears before the Lord as a man; if in truths from the Word it appears as a beautiful man, but if in truths falsified as a monstrous man; the Church so appears from its doctrine and from life according thereto; from which it follows that the doctrine of the Church is its image.
To put an end to the state of the Church, and effect judgment. Signified. AR 645. AR 646.

The Church on earth is to the angelic Heaven as the foundation on which a house rests, or as the feet on which a man stands and with which he walks; wherefore when the Church on earth is destroyed, the Angels lament, and supplicate the Lord to put an end to the Church and raise up a new one. Signified.
The Church in the whole world, and the Church in the Christian world (both consummated). Signified.
Preface. Preparation to disclose the last state of the Church. Treated of. AR 656. AE 926.
The devastation of the Church, and then its end. Signified.
In course of time every Church decreases...
Preparation by the Lord for influx from the inmost Heaven into the Church, in order that its evils and falsities may be universally disclosed, and thus the evil be separated from the good. Signified.
a. More (Divine truth) could not be endured until the end of that Church was seen after its devastation. Signified.
(The argument that the Church is where the Word is, refuted.)
Thus it is made manifest by the Lord that all things of the Church are devastated. Signified.
That Church as to its doctrine entirely destroyed, likewise all the heresies therefrom. Signified.
Hence Jerusalem = the Church as to doctrine in the universal sense.
The bishop nominates a single candidate for the Churches.

It is not said the Roman Catholic Church, but the Roman Catholic religiosity, because they do not approach the Lord or read the Word, and because they invoke the dead; and the Church is the Church from the Lord and the Word, and its perfection is according to the acknowledgement of the Lord, and the understanding of the Word. AR 721.
The Lord's Church, like Heaven, is distinguished into three degrees. Signified, Explained.
No conjunction of good and truth, which makes the Church. Signified.
The Church is the Church from the reception of the Lord's Divine good in the Divine truths which are from Him.
Henceforth a full marriage of the Lord with the Church. Signified, Explained.
The Church is always established first in the Heavens by the Lord, and afterwards through the Heavens on earth.
The Church itself with man is formed through the truths of the Word; not through these truths in the understanding alone, but through a life according to them...
The Church on earth descends from the Lord out of the angelic Heaven. Signified, Explained.
The Church on earth is formed through Heaven by the Lord, in order that they may act and be consociated as one.
The Church is the Church from doctrine and from life according to it.
The Church is founded upon doctrine. Signified.
The Church which is a Church from the Word is in consociation with Heaven and in conjunction with the Lord; not so a Church which is not from the Word.
The acknowledgement and knowledge of the Lord introduce into the Church. Signified.

The Church is one thing and religion another; the Church is called the Church from doctrine, and religion is called religion from life according to doctrine... Yet where there is doctrine and not life, it cannot be said that there is either the Church or religion...
The Apocalypse must be opened at the end of the Church, that some may be saved. Signified.
In the Churches () = before the whole Christian world, because there are the Churches which are here meant.
Heaven and the Church long for the Lord's advent. Signified. AR 960.
The Church here called the bride does not mean the Church from those who are in falsities of faith, but the Church from those who are in truths of faith...
Here, at the end of the Book, the Lord speaks and the Church speaks, as the Bridegroom and the bride.
(On the wedding-day the bride represents the Church.)
There are two things which make the marriage of the Lord and the Church; love and wisdom; and the Lord is love and the Church is wisdom...
After the wedding, both the husband and the wife together represent the Church. CL 125, Explained. CL 126, Explained.

The correspondence of marriage love is with the marriage of the Lord and the Church, that is, as the Lord loves the Church, and wills that the Church should love Him, so a husband and wife mutually love each other. Explained.

The Church is formed by the Lord with the man, and through the man with the wife, and after it has been formed with both it is a full Church, for then there is a full conjunction of good and truth, and the conjunction of good and truth is the Church. The conjunctive inclination, which is marriage love, is in like degree with the conjunction of good and truth which is the Church. CL 125.
Marriage love... is the fundamental of all the loves of Heaven and the Church. Explained.
None can be in this love but those who approach the Lord, love the truths of the Church, and do its goods. Explained.

There are two things which make the Church and thence Heaven with man; the truth of faith and the good of life; the truth of faith causes the Lord's presence, and the good of life according to the truths of faith causes conjunction with Him, and thus the Church and Heaven. Explained.
We saw that the Church with its truths and goods is possible only with those who live in love truly conjugial with one wife, for the marriage of good and truth is the Church with man...
This love is from the Lord according to the reception of good and truth from Him, thus according to the state of the Church.
It is now the end of the Church, because there remains no truth which is not falsified...

As the Church, which is formed through the truth of doctrine; and religion, which is formed through the good of life according to the truth of doctrine; with Christians is only from the Holy Scripture, it is evident that the Church in general and in part is the marriage of good and truth.
On the marriage of the Lord and the Church and its correspondence. General article.
The conjunction of the Lord with the Church, and the reciprocal conjunction of the Church with the Lord, is called marriage. Explained, Illustrated.
The spiritual offspring of the marriage of the Lord with the Church are truths and goods. Explained.
Thus is the Church formed by the Lord with man. Explained.
The Church is from the Lord, and is with those who approach Him, and live according to His commandments. Explained.
The reason marriage love is according to the state of the Church, is that it is according to the state of wisdom with man. Explained.
Those things which are of the Church, and are called spiritual things, reside in the inmost with man. Explained.
Husbands grow cold to their wives when they think vain things against the Lord and the Church.

Varieties of similitudes can be conjoined... especially by conformity in the things of the Church; for by the things of the Church there is effected a conjunction of similitudes which are inwardly apart...
With those who reject... the holy things of the Church, there is no good love...
He said he was a minister of the Church there.
When the Church betroths herself to her Lord (the delights of marriage love will be known).
One cause of this kind of jealousy is the captivity and suffocation of the thoughts in the spiritual things of the Church. Explained.
Uncleanness and cleanness in the Church (are from scortatory and marriage love respectively.) Explained.
(Adulteries) cause men to reject all things of the Church and of religion. Explained.
The love of adultery acts as one with those things which are against the Church.
The marriage of evil and falsity is the Anti-church.
The modern faith has separated religion from the Church. General article.
The Church is the Lord's. Illustrated.
With men who do not acknowledge one God, but several, nothing of the Church coheres together. Explained.
God, from His omnipotence, has established the Church.
Redemption was the subjugation of the Hells and the ordination of the Heavens, and after these things the establishment of the Church.
All the Churches before the Lord's coming were representative Churches, which could only see Divine truths in the shade...
(The difference between the state of the Church before the Lord's coming and after it, described by comparisons.)
When the Church on earth perishes, the lower Heavens also pass away...
Is not the Church the Lord's body, and He its Head? What is a body without a head? or with three heads?
When the primary faith is known... the quality of the Church is known. Example(s).
The men of the Church are in one or other of these three Kingdoms, according to their love, wisdom, and faith.
The Church which is in Divine truths from the Lord will prevail over the Hells. Signified.
The Church is from the Word, and is such with man as is his understanding of the Word. General article.
The reason the Church is according to the understanding of the Word, is that the Church is according to the truths of faith and the goods of charity... These are what essentially make the Church.

The Church is according to its doctrine... yet doctrine does not establish the Church, but the soundness and purity of doctrine, thus the understanding of the Word; but doctrine does not establish and make the special Church which is with each individual man, but faith and life according to it; in like manner the Word does not establish and make the Church in special with man, but faith according to the truths, and life according to the goods which he draws from it and applies to himself.
The Church is not with him who does not confess that the Lord is the Son of God. Illustrated.
Hence the Church is called the body of Christ.

They who reject either the Word or the Lord reject the Church, because the Church is from the Lord through the Word; and they who reject the Church are out of Heaven, for the Church introduces into Heaven.
The Church is the neighbour which is to beloved in a higher degree. General article.
The Lord's Kingdom means the Church in the whole world, which is called the communion of saints; and also means Heaven.
The Church in the Heavens and on earth is the Lord's body.

The spiritual pay taxes from goodwill, because they are for the preservation of their country and the Church, and for administration by the office-bearers and governors, whose salaries and stipends are to be paid out of the public treasury...
Repentance is the first of the Church with man. General article.
The communion called the Church consists of all men in whom is the Church; and the Church enters with man while he is being regenerated...
That the Church is not with man until sins are removed; shown by comparisons.
After redemption, the Lord established a new Church; in like manner He also establishes the things of the Church with man, and makes him a Church in particular.
Without truths there can be no theology, and where this is not, neither is there the Church.
So also is the Church on earth ordered by the Lord.
The Holy Supper contains all things of the Church. General article.
The essentials of the Church are three; God, charity, and faith...
As baptism is introduction into the Church...
The consummation of the age is the last time or end of the Church. General article.
When truth is consummated in the Church, good is also consummated there, and then the Church has an end.
(Why the Church passes through circles of progress and decay.)
The Church appears before the Lord as a man, and this Grand Man passes through ages of his own.

I have heard that the Churches which are in different goods and truths, provided their goods relate to love to the Lord, and their truths to faith in the Lord, are like so many jewels in a king's crown.
The man who is in faith in the Lord, and in charity towards the neighbour, is a Church in particular; the Church in general is composed of such. TCR 775, Explained.

In the Church there are general and particular, and also most general things, and hence it is that four Churches have preceded in order, from which progression has originated the most general principle of the Church, and successively what is general and particular of each one.
No former Church was in the truth. Explained.
(On the successive Churches.)
Societies of the true Church, in which all are brethren.
What is said in the Word in relation to the ancient Churches applies also to the present ones.
That the Lord's Church is very greatly promoted by the evil...
Both preacher and hearer are in a very different state when they are in Church.

On the influx of the Lord into the Church... The Lord's Church is like the heart and lungs. Explained. The Angels dwell with those who are in love to the Lord and towards the neighbour, but when there is no Church the Angels are removed. The consequence of this.
Everyone thinks the doctrines of his own Church true, therefore in whatever Church a man he born, he ought to examine the Word...
The Church which now perishes in Europe will be established in Africa.
On the Churches in the other life.
a. On the wicked there who want to make one Church out of many.
How one Church may really be made.
Such distinguish Churches according to mere truths.
How it is that the Church represents the heart and lungs.
To the seven Churches = to all those who are in truths from good. Explained. AE 21. AE 58. AE 90. AE 91. AE 108.
The Church is not the Church from what is proper to man, but from what is Divine of the Lord.
The light of intelligence does not make the Church with man, but the reception of the light in heat.
The seven Churches = all who are of the Lord's Church, thus the Church in general. AE 150:3. AE 256. Explained, Enumerated.
The good of love and of faith makes the Church with man.
As Heaven and the Church make one by correspondence, it is said write to the Angel of the Church; and also because there must be such a correspondence for the Church to be the Church with man.
Everything of the Church is from the Lord, and in fact from His Divine Human. Signified. AE 151, Explained.
The Church would be one, and not many as at this day, if all were regarded from charity, although they might differ as to doctrinal and ritual things. References.
Those with whom the internal man is closed are not men of the Church, for the Church with man is formed through communication with Heaven...
The Church is in man as Heaven is in an Angel; and every Church is constituted of those who are of the Church.
Intromission into the Church. Signified.
The two principal things of the Church are to acknowledge the Divine Human and apply the truths of the Word to life...

Faith from the Lord as to the appearance is the first of the Church, but charity itself is actually the first of the Church, because this makes the Church with man. There are two things which make the Church; charity and faith...
The Church in special is where the Word is, and where by the Word the Lord is known. Explained.
Love makes Heaven, and therefore it makes the Church.
The nascent Church. Signified.
The conjunction of good and truth makes Heaven with man while he lives on earth...

The Lord's Church is diffused through the whole world, but its inmost is where the Lord is known and acknowledged, and where the Word is; from that inmost, light and intelligence are propagated to all who are around and are of the Church, but this propagation of light and intelligence is effected in Heaven.
To acknowledge the Divine in the Lord's Human is the primary of the Church, by which there is conjunction; and as it is the primary it is also the first of the Church. Signified.
The Lord's Church is universal; it is with all who are in the good of life, and who from their doctrine look to Heaven, and who by it conjoin themselves with the Lord.
Manifestation of the states of those who are of the Church where the Word is. Treated of.
It is said the Church where the Word is, because the Lord's Church is in the whole world, but in special where the Word is...

The Church in the whole world is before the Lord as one man, for it makes one with the angelic Heaven... In this man the Church where the Word is is as the heart and lungs, the Church with those who are in celestial love is as the heart, and with those in spiritual love as the lungs... thus all in the whole world who constitute the universal Church, live from the Church where the Word is...
These successive states of the Church do not appear to anyone in the world...
This is the origin of all dissensions and heresies in the Church... DWis 11.

It is said the Church with man, because the Church is in man, for the Church is the Church from charity and faith, and these are in man, and if they are not there, the Church is not with him. It is believed that the Church is where the Word is and the Lord is known, but the Church is only from those who at heart acknowledge the Lord's Divine, and who learn truths from the Lord through the Word, and do them; the rest do not constitute the Church.
The Church is in man, and from the men in whom the Church is.
The internal of the Church is the good of love and the good of faith, and its external is worship thence.
In the Lord's Church there is an internal and there is an external; the internal of the Church is charity and faith thence; the external of the Church is the good of life...
The four Churches, from the Most Ancient to the Jewish, were represented by the image seen by Nebuchadnezzar. Enumerated.
The Church regarded in itself is in the internal man, but the external Church is in the external man; which however act as one, as cause and effect.
There are two things which make the Church; the truth of doctrine and the good of life; there must be both with man for him to be of the Church. These two are represented by Ephraim and Manasseh.
Good is what makes the Church...
There was then a like state of the Church in the Spiritual World as in the natural world...
The state of the man of the Church about its end is here described; that from internal or spiritual it would become external or sensuous; yet it would not perish altogether...
The state of the Church at its very end. Treated of. AE 569:9, Described. AE 570, Described. AE 602. AE 614. AE 624.
The place of feet () = the Church; for the Lord's Church is with men in the natural world... Hence the Church is also called the Lord's footstool. Illustrated.
Porch and court = all things outside the Church, but which regard it... For the Church itself is in the internal man.
These doctrines will be preached about the end of the Church... When the end of the Church is at hand, the interiors of the Word, etc., are revealed and taught... AE 644.
The successive states of the Churches on our Earth have been like those of a man who is being regenerated. Explained.
The end of the Church, when the Lord's Divine is no longer acknowledged, and therefore there is no good and truth. Signified. AE 649:3.
From the conjunction (of the spiritual and natural minds), man is a man of the Church.
Thus man founds the Church with himself.
The Church is first formed with man through knowledges in the natural man.
Anxiety caused by the two witnesses in the devastated Church. Signified.
The state of the Church at its end, when it is provided that a sudden change should not do harm to those who are to be separated. Treated of.
At the end of the Church the interiors of the Word are manifested...
A remarkable change of the state of the interiors with those who are of the Church. Signified, Explained. See AE 670:end.

At the end of the Church, when the Last Judgment is at hand, they who are spiritually good are taken away from those who are only naturally so, and then all truths and good and understanding of truth are also taken away from the latter. Signified, Explained.
The third woe () involves the last state of the Church... and the state of separation then of the good and the evil, and at length the Last Judgment.
To judge all according to the truths of their own Church. Signified.
The spiritual captivity in which the faithful are when they remain in a Church where there is no longer any truth or good. Signified.
Quality of the man of the Church at its end.

The Spirits who are with man are from those who have been in the faith of their own Church while on earth, and no Spirits receive the doctrine of the New Church but those who have been in the spiritual affection of truth... The number of these increases daily in the World of Spirits...
The two principles of evil and falsity into which the Church successively falls. AE 879:2.
When the doctrine disagrees with the Word it is no longer a Church, but a religiosity which counterfeits the Church.
